Beyond the obvious · twice-weekly edit

Unusual London events,
this week.

Discover free and affordable things to do in London this week and weekend, selected for unusual access, local character and a story worth following. Every listing is checked against the official organiser before publication.

Friday 6 November – Sunday 8 November · Last edited 2 November at 15:19

The complete edit

6 verified events
Friday 6 November1 event
Talk Free

12:00–13:00

Women’s War Work: Indian Women and the Second World War

Historian Kiran Sahota uncovers the overlooked work of Indian women in wartime services, from the Women’s Auxiliary Corps to the Wasbies in Burma and naval support roles.

Venue
National Army Museum
Address
Royal Hospital Road, Chelsea, London, SW3 4HT
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Saturday 7 November1 event
Community Free

10:30–17:00

Diwali at the National Maritime Museum

Greenwich’s museum becomes a free community festival of South Asian dance, music, storytelling, gallery talks, craft workshops and a closing lantern parade into the park.

Venue
National Maritime Museum
Address
Romney Road, Greenwich, London, SE10 9NF
Access
Booking recommended
Check official details ↗
Sunday 8 November4 events
Art & design Free

11:00–18:00

This Must Be the Place: Artists for Whitechapel Gallery

On its final day, 23 artists fill the former Whitechapel Library’s Assembly Room with new painting, marking 125 years of the East End gallery and supporting its future.

Venue
Whitechapel Gallery, Assembly Room
Address
77–82 Whitechapel High Street, London, E1 7QX
Access
Drop in
Check official details ↗
Heritage & history £10; £8 concessions

13:45–16:30

Remembering Wartime Willesden

Inside Willesden Jewish Cemetery, a judge and local volunteers recover stories of chaplains, artists, Bletchley Park contributors and residents who sacrificed their lives in wartime.

Venue
Willesden Jewish Cemetery
Address
Beaconsfield Road, Willesden, London, NW10 2JE
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Local culture Free

14:15–15:15

Afternoon Poems: The Poetry of Decadence

Poetry ambassadors read the opulent, rebellious and fantastical verse of Wilde, Baudelaire and Beardsley inside the Hampstead house where John Keats lived and wrote.

Venue
Keats House
Address
10 Keats Grove, Hampstead, London, NW3 2RR
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
Local culture £12 standard incl. levy

15:00–16:30

A History of Black People and Alternative Music

Big Joanie founder Stephanie Phillips restores Black artists to the history of punk, rock and alternative music, from Sister Rosetta Tharpe to Poly Styrene and today’s experimental scene.

Venue
Conway Hall, Brockway Room
Address
25 Red Lion Square, London, WC1R 4RL
Access
Booking required
Check official details ↗
